blocks.text: `std.can` provides CAN bus frames (classic 8 bytes, CAN FD 64 bytes), the 15-bit CRC of classic CAN and the SAE J1939 identifier layout used in trucks, ships and engines. It does no allocation and needs no libc.

**`std.mmio`** reads and writes memory-mapped hardware registers with `volatile` access: the compiler never drops, merges or reorders the accesses. **`std.hal`** defines driver interfaces shared by boards (`OutputPin`, `I2c`, `SpiBus`, `Uart`, `Delay`); a driver takes the interface it needs as a generic parameter and runs on any board. For testing there are `MockPin`, `MockBus`, `MockDelay`.

blocks.text: Bare-metal programs are built with `gg build --no-std --target cortex-m4 --linker-script link.ld`; `gg new --template cortex-m` sets up a ready skeleton. For the stack limit there is `gg stack-usage` and the options `--forbid-heap --forbid-recursion --max-stack 1024`.
